prerequisites: It would be convenient for the student, in their previous studies before University, to have taken scientific-technological oriented subjects such as: mathematics, physics, mechanics, electrotechnics, industrial technology, etc.

learning_outcomes.text: Recognize and understand the general laws of applied physics (mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism) that apply to engineering.
Apply the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism to solve engineering problems.
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful for successfully solving new situations related to industrial engineering.
Act effectively in a multilingual and multidisciplinary team.
Ability to perform laboratory setups and experiments.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of industrial technical engineering.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in diverse situations or before diverse audiences.
Apply knowledge specific to industrial engineering in learning new methods and theories.
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem critically and constructively.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. INTRODUCTION. International system units. Thermodynamics and heat transfer. Principles of calorimetry. Energy balances. Problems.

Topic 2. HEAT TRANSFER MECHANISMS. Heat transfer: Conduction: Fourier's Law and thermal conductivity. Convection: types of convection and Newton's Law. Heat transfer: Radiation. Radiation: Stefan-Boltzmann Law and radiative balance between two surfaces. Simultaneous heat transfer mechanisms. Problems.

Topic 3. STEADY-STATE HEAT TRANSFER. Steady transfer in flat walls. Concept of thermal resistance. Network of series, parallel, and mixed thermal resistances in flat walls. Steady-state heat transfer in cylinders and spheres: conduction. Network of thermal resistances in cylinders and spheres. Critical radius of insulation. Nusselt number. Thermal boundary layer. Prandtl number. Laminar and turbulent flow: Reynolds number. Properties and laws of radiation. Problems.

Topic 4. HEAT CONDUCTION EQUATION. Steady and transient heat transfer. One-dimensional and multidimensional thermal conduction. Heat generation. One-dimensional conduction in a flat wall, in a cylinder, and in a sphere. General conduction equation. Boundary conditions in conduction. Conduction-convection boundary conditions. Conduction-radiation boundary conditions. Examples of one-dimensional conduction in steady state. Heat generation in a solid. Convective transfer to the environment of heat generated by a solid. Conductive transfer to a pipe of heat generated inside it. Variable thermal conductivity. Problems.

Topic 5. HEAT EXCHANGERS. Types of heat exchangers. Overall heat transfer coefficient. Fouling factor. Analysis of Heat Exchangers. Heat transfer rate in an isolated exchanger. Heat transfer rate in a phase change. Log Mean Temperature Difference - LMTD Method. Double tube and Parallel flow. Flow and Counterflow. Double tube and Counterflow. Exchanger Selection. Effectiveness - NTU Method. Effectiveness Relationships. NTU Relationships. Selection of Heat Exchangers. Problems.

Topic 1: COULOMB'S LAW. ELECTRIC FORCES AND FIELDS. Coulomb's Law. Force created by different charge configurations on point charges. Definition and origin of electric field. Electric field lines and flux. Electric field created by different charge configurations at a point. Field created by a uniformly charged straight and infinite conductor. Field created by different charged conductors: longitudinal, surface, and volumetric. Problems.

Topic 2: GAUSS'S LAW. Introduction. Field lines, rules. Electric flux. Gauss's Theorem. Applications of Gauss's Law to the calculation of electric fields. Application to the calculation of electric fields created by different charge configurations. Problems.

Topic 3: MAGNETISM. MAGNETIC FIELDS AND FORCES. Definition and origin. Lines of induction and magnetic flux. Effects of magnetic fields, Lorentz Force and Laplace's Law. Effects of a constant and uniform magnetic field on a current loop, electromagnetic torque. Magnetic field created by moving charges, current element and infinite conductors at a point P, Biot-Savart Law. Magnetic force between two parallel conductors. Magnetic field created by a loop. Magnetic field created by a solenoid. Magnetic field created by a toroidal winding. Ampere's Law, application to the calculation of magnetic fields. Displacement current and generalized Ampere's Law. Gauss's Law of magnetism. Problems.
Topic 4: INDUCED ELECTROMOTIVE FORCE. Introduction. Induced electromotive force. Faraday's Law. Elementary AC and DC generator. Lenz's Law. Eddy currents. Maxwell's Equations.
Topic 5: INDUCTANCE. Coefficient of mutual induction. Coefficient of self-induction. Association of coils in series. Coupling coefficient between coils. Magnetic energy. Problems.

Topic 6: MAGNETIC PROPERTIES OF MATTER. MAGNETIC CIRCUITS. Classification of substances according to their magnetic properties: diamagnetic, paramagnetic, and ferromagnetic substances. Magnetomotive force. Magnetic circuits. Types of magnetic circuits. Magnetic permeability. Relative permeability. Relationship between electrical and magnetic circuits. Association of reluctances. Magnetic field intensity. B-H curves. Hysteresis loop of a ferromagnetic material. Problems.
Practice 1: BASIC ELECTRICITY LABORATORY. Sources, basic passive elements, measuring equipment.
Practice 2: THE MULTIMETER. Assembly of basic DC and AC electrical circuits. Measurement and calculation of parameters and magnitudes in circuits.
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
assessment_rules: The evaluation consists of 'Other forms of evaluation' (20%), 'Practical cases' (20%), and 'Mixed tests' (60%). 'Other forms of evaluation' include continuous assessment activities such as assignments, problems in seminars, or questionnaires. 'Practical cases' assess attendance at practices and laboratory reports. 'Mixed tests' combine development questions, objective questions, short questions, and/or multiple-choice tests, covering both Heat and Electromagnetism blocks.
